newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST - Spain one-year bill yields to dip sharply.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Spain one-year bill yields to dip sharply.

text.p: Spain's one-year Treasury bill yields are expected to fall at an auction on Wednesday to around 5.30 percent amid heavy demand, analysts said on Tuesday.
At the previous auction on April 2 the yield was 5.59 percent.
Earlier on Tuesday, Spain's central bank sanctioned its third rate cut this year, dropping the key money market rate at its regular repurchase auction by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.

"A week ago the market started having different expectations about interest rates. Tomorrow at the auction we'll see high demand and marginal rates of around 5.30 percent, or even lower," a dealer said.
Earlier this morning, one-year bills were trading in the grey market at around 5.26 to 5.30 percent.
This week there are one-year bills maturing for a total of 603 billion pesetas and traders are expecting new issuance for around 500 and 600 billion pesetas.
"In these months, the Treasury is facing a high level of maturing bills. But market conditions seem favourable," said a dealer.
One-year bill yields hit a historic low on January 22, at 5.052 percent.
